candidate_relations.reason: Mitral-valve prolapse can click, but a loud left-sternal sound audible without a stethoscope after pleuritic pain is not MVP.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: mitral-valve click vs extra-cardiac Hamman sign

candidate_relations.reason: Pericarditis is a different entity; inflammatory markers, ECG, and troponin were normal.
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is unrelated to inspiratory precordial pain with a recorded Hamman click and normal ECG.
Pulmonary embolism is a different diagnosis; D-dimer and gas exchange were normal.
Tietze syndrome is inflammatory costochondral swelling, not a Hamman click after acute pleuritic pain.
Costochondritis does not produce a loud extra-cardiac click recorded at the left sternal edge.
Precordial catch is a benign stabbing pain syndrome without Hamman sign or a thin-body-habitus pneumothorax context.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: precordial catch vs primary spontaneous pneumothorax

case_quality_flags: No candidate names pneumothorax; Hamman click in a thin young man with pleuritic pain is the classic small left pneumothorax/pneumomediastinum presentation even when the chest radiograph is reported normal
